reason: Both muscles need living muscle tissue, so developing cells look like a useful starting point. I don't yet know how they become the tissue needed here.
expectation: The compatibility list should show how the developing cells can be used to build muscle tissue.

alternatives.reason: The two tissues might form muscle together, but their precise roles aren't yet clear.

effect: The cells and supporting tissue formed muscle bundles, which can now fill a muscle's outer covering.
reaction: The picture makes the connection between muscle fibres and tendons clearer.
reason: The biceps covering has an unfilled space, and the muscle bundles look like they belong inside it.
expectation: The bundles should fill the biceps covering and form a biceps muscle.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs muscle bundles, so I could build it first.

effect: The bundles filled the biceps covering, forming a muscle with tendons ready to attach.
reaction: The picture makes the path from muscle to tendon clear.
reason: The goal calls for connecting the biceps across the front of the elbow, so the arm skeleton is the natural next pairing.
expectation: The biceps tendons should attach to the skeleton across the front of the elbow.

effect: The biceps is attached across the front of the elbow, leaving the back muscle slot empty.
reaction: The two poses show how the shortening biceps bends the elbow.
reason: The triceps covering has an unfilled space, just as the biceps covering did, so it should take the muscle bundles.
expectation: The bundles should fill the covering and form a triceps with tendons.

effect: The muscle bundles formed a triceps with tendons, ready to fill the back muscle slot.
reaction: The picture shows how the muscle's supporting tissue continues into the tendon.
reason: The arm assembly has an empty back muscle slot, and the triceps belongs across the back of the elbow.
expectation: The triceps should attach to the back of the arm assembly.

effect: The completed arm shows how the triceps pulls to straighten the elbow, opposite the biceps' pull to bend it.
reaction: The two poses make the opposite pulls easier to picture.

mostWorthwhile.text: Attaching the triceps was most worthwhile because it completed the comparison: both muscles pull, but their attachments turn the joint in opposite directions.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps repeated the biceps assembly in a predictable way, although it reinforced that both use the same tissue.

surprise.text: I hadn't understood how developing muscle cells and supporting tissue made bundles, or how the supporting tissue carried their pull toward tendons.

arbitrary.text: The first pairing wasn't obvious to me: I needed the compatibility hint to see that developing muscle cells and supporting tissue went together. The resulting picture explained its purpose.

continue.text: I would try another chapter if it built on these connections. Seeing the parts assembled into movements was more interesting than the repeated muscle-building step.
